problems.problem: The upper field rendered as a photographic brick-WALL texture (visible mortar joints and brick courses across the whole top band) instead of the declared flat silkscreen ink plane; the concept material is 'two flat silkscreen ink planes... no plaster, no photographic depth', and the prompt itself forbids texture. The literal brick pattern adds photographic depth and visual noise that fights the flat terracotta rectangle and the flat gray field.
problems.root_cause: Background prompt wording ('muted brick ink plane') was interpreted literally as masonry by the scene generator.
problems.repair_strategy: Regenerate with a prompt describing only empty flat matte color fields and even diffuse light, removing the word 'brick' so no masonry texture is synthesized.

problems.problem: The busy mortar-grid texture sits directly behind the title column (title bbox x59-285, y403-558 lies entirely inside the textured band), so the dark ink characters compete with hundreds of small mortar edges; references 3-5 keep type on clean flat fields. The texture band's lower edge also cuts through the title's descender zone at y~558, creating an accidental second horizontal division right under the headline.
problems.root_cause: Textured plane placed in the type zone instead of a flat value field.
problems.repair_strategy: Flatten the upper field (prompt regeneration) so the headline rests on one calm value; keep title position and ink.

problems.problem: The hinge rule (decoration line at y=674) reads correctly at the collar on the upright case, but the same line visibly slices across the lying cap's body at left (line passes through the cap silhouette region around x300-700 at y674 in canvas terms) and terminates abruptly at the terracotta rectangle's left edge x=540, so the 'single printed rule' looks like three disconnected strokes (gray field segment, rectangle segment, collar segment) rather than one continuous hinge line.
problems.root_cause: Decoration line width/position not coordinated with the rectangle edge and the cap silhouette.
problems.repair_strategy: Re-place the rule so it runs as one uninterrupted stroke from the left margin to the rectangle's left edge only, stopping before the product, or extend it fully behind the product; adjust decoration x/width accordingly.

problems.problem: Three horizontal divisions stack in the upper half: texture-band bottom (~y560), rectangle top (y346) and rectangle bottom (y1037), plus the rule at y674; the texture band's bottom edge and the rectangle's top edge are close but not aligned, producing a ragged double horizon on the left half that reads as an accident rather than the intended single clean division.
problems.root_cause: Generated texture band boundary does not coincide with the deterministic rectangle geometry.
problems.repair_strategy: Regenerate background so the only horizontal division is the one flat plane change; align perceived division with the rectangle top edge by making the whole upper field one flat tone.

problems.problem: Title wraps as '立处,即 / 是分分界' style two-line stack with the comma forcing an awkward break ('立处,即' / '是分界'), and at 68px inside max_width 250 the column feels cramped against the left margin while the subtitle (26px, three ragged lines ending in a lone '点。' orphan line) dissipates; against references 3-5 the type block lacks a confident optical axis and the orphan widow line is an amateur tell.
problems.root_cause: max_width too narrow for the title phrase and subtitle line_height/width producing a widow.
problems.repair_strategy: Widen title max_width so the break falls after the comma naturally, and widen subtitle max_width to avoid the single-character last line; keep copy, font, color and left alignment.

problems.problem: In the contact detail crop (image 6) both the upright case base and the lying cap DO sit on the gray field with soft dark contact shadows present at y~1206 and y~1238, so grounding is not absent; however at opacity 0.35 with blur 10 the shadows read as faint smudges against the flat silkscreen concept and the cap's shadow detaches slightly at its right end, leaving the cap's far edge looking marginally lifted.
problems.root_cause: Shadow opacity/blur tuned below what the glossy cutout's baked-in near-shadowless studio light needs on a flat field.
problems.repair_strategy: Raise contact shadow opacity modestly and tighten blur so both contact points read as deliberate printed contact, keeping offset_y at 0.

creative_diversity_evidence.evidence: All four propositions keep the identical visual constant: the single untouched lipstick cutout standing isolated on the source's neutral gray ground with only a floor contact shadow, while flat primitives are parked strictly behind it. Within that constant, c1 (one enlarged original-alpha silhouette offset behind), c3 (eight flat discs in a rising arc behind) and c4 (four窄 stepped champagne rectangles behind) produce the same actual visual event - a flat monochrome graphic shape or shape-stack hovering behind an isolated packshot - differing only in primitive type, count and arrangement, i.e. renamed materials and palette swaps, not different advertising ideas. c2 does stage a genuinely different event (a horizontal field division plus the single straight line intersected by the upright case and lying cap, reading the collar as hinge), so it survives. Execution audit: each concept uses one photographed product instance, no rotation, no diptych, no macro crop; primitive counts (1 silhouette; 1 rectangle + 1 line; 8 ellipses; 4 rectangles) sit inside the eight-primitive ceiling with the line budget spent only once; no efficacy, ingredient, price or newness claims; packaging, collar and bullet unaltered. Feasibility is therefore not the failure point - conceptual redundancy is.
creative_diversity_evidence.required_revision: Keep c2 as the sole flat-geometry-behind-packshot direction. Rebuild two of the three collapsed concepts so the visible event changes category rather than primitive count: e.g. convert one into a source-compatible generated environment occupying the whole backdrop (gradient hero field or architectural plane corner with cast shadow logic consistent with the source's soft diffuse light, product still unrotated and fully visible), and convert another into a dense full-frame field event (flat ellipse discs filling the canvas around and behind the product as an environment, not a sparse arc), while retiring the offset-silhouette ghost or the stepped gauge entirely. Do not add slogans, brand history, relighting, second photographs, macro crops or diptychs; retain the locked title 'BEAUTY' as the only verbal layer count permits.
